case_title: BHAGWAN SINGH v. STATE OF UTTARAKHAND
aggravating_circumstances: Firing a gun at a crowded place during a marriage ceremony, knowledge of the danger involved
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 302 and 307 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment and 5 years’ rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Acquitted for offence under Section 25 of the Arms Act, but upheld conviction under Sections 302 and 307 IPC
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was present at a marriage ceremony where he fired a licensed gun towards the roof, resulting in the death of two individuals and injuries to three others. The gun was loaded with live cartridges, and the firing occurred in a crowded area. The prosecution alleged that the accused aimed the gun at a specific person, but the evidence showed that the gun was fired towards the roof, leading to an accidental misfiring. The accused was initially convicted under Sections 302 and 307 of the IPC, but the conviction was modified to Sections 304-II and 308 of the IPC. The accused was sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 20,000.
